# Kazakhstan

Wealth gradients in fertility and mortality: the values for an OG-Core calibration, followed by the estimates they are based on. Terms are defined in the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −0.78, by age as below | MICS 2015, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | −0.92 | DHS 1999, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | 2.97 − 0.432 × ln(GDP per capita, PPP) | [general gradient](../methods/general-gradient.md), GDP per capita in constant 2021 international $; for example −0.31 at $2,000 and −1.01 at $10,000, each with a 95% prediction interval of about ±0.7 |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Values are [wealth gradients](../glossary.md#wealth-gradient). Before they are passed to OG-Core, each is divided by 100 × (1 − p), where p is OG-Core's rate at that age ([details](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility gradient by age of mother** (`fert_gradient`; ages below 15 use the 15–19 value, ages 50 and above the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.56 | −0.88 | −0.57 | −0.46 | −0.69 | −1.17 | −1.76 |

**Adult and child mortality gradient by age** (`mort_gradient`; ages 15–59: the general-gradient value for this country plus the pooled offset for each band ([age pattern](../methods/general-gradient.md#age-pattern)); ages 5–14 use the 15–29 value; ages 60–74 fall in a straight line from the 45–59 value to 0 at age 75; ages 75 and above, and OG-Core's final age, use 0):

| 1–4 | 5–14 | 15–29 | 30–44 | 45–59 | 60–74 | 75+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.55 (DHS 1999) | value − 0.41 | value − 0.41 | value − 0.18 | value + 0.21 | the 45–59 value at 60, falling to 0 at 75 | 0 |

Ages 1–4 use the country's own gradient in child mortality at ages 1–4 (DHS), or, where there is none, its under-five gradient plus a pooled offset ([details](../methods/general-gradient.md#age-pattern)). Infant mortality (age 0) is `infmort_gradient`, above.

*Note:* The most recent survey with infant mortality by wealth quintile is from 1999. Gradients can change substantially over such a period; state the survey year when using this value.

## Estimates

### Household surveys

Latest Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) or Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) with a complete wealth-quintile breakdown, for each indicator ([`gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv); earlier surveys in `gradient_library.csv`). MICS rates are taken from the World Bank's compilation of survey results by wealth quintile ([sources](../sources.md)).

| Indicator | Survey | Lowest | Second | Middle | Fourth | Highest | Low/high ratio | Gradient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total fertility rate (births per woman) | MICS 2015 | 3.5 | 3.9 | 3.6 | 2.5 | 2 | 1.75 | −0.78 |
| Infant mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 1999 | 68 | 65 | 66 | 27 | 42 | 1.62 | −0.92 |
| Under-five mortality rate (per 1,000 live births) | DHS 1999 | 82 | 73 | 72 | 36 | 45 | 1.82 | −0.95 |
| Child mortality, ages 1–4 (per 1,000 children aged 1) | DHS 1999 | 15 | 8 | 7 | 9 | 3 | 5.00 | −1.55 |
